source.title: Over-Parameterized Deep Neural Networks Have No Strict Local Minima For Any Continuous Activations
source.authors: Da-Wei Li; Tian Ding; Ruo-Yu Sun

record.file_problem: The supplied text is the full paper, though its title differs from the provided TITLE: the text is titled “On the Benefit of Width for Neural Networks: Disappearance of Basins.”
record.tranche_reason: The paper proves results about how width relates to bad basins in neural-network loss landscapes. It uses theoretical arguments and constructed examples rather than testing gradient-based training or classification error.
record.gate_note: The paper reports theoretical results about loss landscapes and a constructed numerical example. It does not report CIFAR benchmarks, random initialization training outcomes, or gradient-descent convergence. Cited empirical findings from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study proves existence or absence of compact, set-wise strict local minima. This differs from V2's frequency of gradient descent reaching spurious minima in realizable ReLU teacher-student problems. It neither measures those training outcomes nor gives an argument contradicting them. Its own results test none of V1–V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors prove that sufficient width eliminates sub-optimal compact basins under their assumptions and construct narrow-network counterexamples for several activation classes. They do not establish a transition for every activation or guarantee gradient-descent convergence.
record.recipe_differences: The paper proves loss-landscape properties and constructs counterexamples; it does not run gradient-based training from random initialization or measure classification error.
record.method_sensitivity: The basin result depends on width, activation class, and architecture. Positive homogeneous activations have no set-wise strict local minima at any width; other stated activation classes admit constructed narrow-network basins.

fits_no_version.finding: Under the stated data and convex-loss assumptions, sufficiently wide fully connected networks have no sub-optimal compact basins; an earlier wide layer also suffices with the specified pyramid and monotonicity conditions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Width at least the sample count can eliminate sub-optimal compact basins under specified architectural conditions.

fits_no_version.finding: Constructed narrow networks and labels can produce sub-optimal basins, including a numerical single-neuron Swish example.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Some narrow networks admit bad basins for suitably chosen activations or labels.

fits_no_version.finding: Positive-homogeneous scaling symmetry rules out compact set-wise strict local minima at every width, without ruling out non-strict spurious local minima.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Absence of compact basins in positive-homogeneous networks does not imply absence of optimizer traps.

record.problems: The positive and negative results are theoretical and concern set-wise strict local minima, not whether a specified optimizer reaches low training error. The narrow-network counterexamples use constructed output data. The computational Swish example uses a constructed dataset and parameters. No empirical training benchmark or uncertainty estimate is reported.

untested.parts: All parts: convolutional-network training error on CIFAR-10/100, including random or corrupted labels and recipe-dependent failures.

All parts: realizable ReLU teacher-student problems, gradient descent from standard initialization, failure frequency as widths grow, and reductions from one or two extra student neurons at widths 6–20.
All parts: depth-dependent training degradation, identity shortcuts, and the stated initialization exceptions.
All parts: initialization-dependent propagation, learning speed and trainable depth.
All parts: learning-rate stability thresholds, loss and curvature dynamics, recovery and divergence.
All parts: batch-normalization effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: The extracted theorem statements are related landscape results, not partial observations of V2. In particular, the positive-homogeneous result is compatible with spurious ReLU local minima because the paper's basin definition requires compactness.

versions.untested_parts: Training error on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, random or corrupted labels, optimizer, initialization, model size, and training duration.

The frequency of gradient descent ending in spurious minima as teacher and student grow together; the effect of adding one or two neurons in teacher-student ReLU problems; tested widths of 6 to 20 neurons.
Depth effects in plain versus residual convolutional networks and training outcomes with shortcuts, special initializations, or Fixup.
Activation-matched initialization, signal or gradient propagation, training speed, trainable depth, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, and 10,000-layer convolutional training.
Training dynamics at learning rates above or near stability limits, including loss, curvature, sharpness, and divergence.
Batch normalization effects on training speed, accuracy, and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup training without normalization.

rows.subject: fully connected neural network
rows.size_stated: Last hidden layer width dH ≥ N, where N is the number of training samples
rows.operation_detail: Theorem 2 establishes that the empirical loss has no sub-optimal set-wise strict local minima for any continuous activations.

conditions.value: Nonzero, distinct input samples; convex loss with respect to predictions
Continuous
Last hidden layer has at least N neurons

rows.measure: Existence of sub-optimal set-wise strict local minima (bad basins)
rows.value: No sub-optimal set-wise strict local minima
rows.note: A theoretical result about the loss landscape; it does not establish that gradient training reaches a global minimum or low training error.
rows.check: Theorem 2 establishes absence of sub-optimal compact basins when the last hidden layer has at least N neurons. It does not establish absence of all spurious local minima or successful gradient-descent training as specified in V2.

rows.subject: fully connected neural network
rows.size_stated: A wide layer has at least N neurons; subsequent layers form a non-increasing-width pyramid
rows.operation_detail: Theorem 3 establishes the absence of sub-optimal basins under additional structural and activation assumptions.

conditions.value: Nonzero, distinct inputs
Convex with respect to predictions
Continuous; activations after the wide layer are non-increasing or non-decreasing
Non-increasing widths after a layer of width at least N

rows.measure: Existence of sub-optimal set-wise strict local minima (bad basins)
rows.value: No sub-optimal set-wise strict local minima
rows.note: A theoretical landscape result under the stated pyramid and activation conditions.
rows.check: Theorem 3 concerns compact basins under width, pyramid-architecture and monotonicity assumptions, without teacher-student training or optimizer outcomes.

rows.subject: 1-hidden-layer neural network
rows.operation_detail: Theorem 4 constructs output data for which the network has a sub-optimal basin.

conditions.value: Input vector has no zero or identical entries
There exist output data y producing the result
Theorem 4 does not restrict activation beyond the construction

rows.value: A sub-optimal basin exists for some output data
rows.note: Existence for constructed output data does not report how often gradient descent finds such a basin.
rows.check: Theorem 4 constructs both an activation function and output data producing a bad basin for m < N. The activation condition should state this existential construction; it is not a result for arbitrary fixed activations or ReLU teacher-student training.

rows.subject: 1-hidden-layer neural network
rows.operation_detail: Theorem 5 proves that positive homogeneous activations have no set-wise strict local minima for any data.

conditions.value: Positive homogeneous: σ(αt) = ασ(t) for α > 0
Any data (x, y)

rows.measure: Existence of set-wise strict local minima
rows.value: No set-wise strict local minima at any width
rows.note: This result identifies an activation class without the narrow-to-wide basin transition described for other classes.
rows.check: Theorem 5 excludes compact set-wise strict local minima through positive-homogeneous scaling symmetry. Non-strict spurious local minima and gradient-descent failure remain possible, so this neither limits nor challenges V2.

rows.subject: 1-hidden-layer neural network
rows.operation_detail: Theorem 6 constructs output data giving a sub-optimal basin for a twice continuously differentiable activation.

conditions.value: σ(0), σ′(0), and σ″(0) are nonzero
Inputs have no zero or identical entries
There exist output data y producing the result

rows.value: A sub-optimal basin exists for some output data
rows.note: An existential result for a narrow network and a specified activation class.
rows.check: Theorem 6 is an existence result for constructed labels and a smooth activation with three nonzero derivatives/values at zero. It does not measure V2's ReLU teacher-student behavior.

rows.subject: 1-hidden-layer neural network
rows.operation_detail: Theorem 7 constructs data for which piecewise-linear activations with the stated behavior at zero yield a sub-optimal basin.

conditions.value: Piecewise linear with σ(0) = σ′(0) = 0
A positive-measure set of input data; there exist output data y producing the result

rows.value: A sub-optimal basin exists for a positive-measure set of inputs and some output data
rows.note: The result is existential over output data and applies only under the stated conditions.
rows.check: Theorem 7 constructs bad basins for piecewise-linear activations flat around zero under 2m + 1 ≤ N. It does not establish gradient-descent failure frequencies or the effect of adding neurons relative to a teacher.

rows.subject: 1-hidden-layer single-neuron Swish network
rows.operation_detail: The paper computationally constructs a sub-optimal strict local minimum for a particular Swish network and dataset.

conditions.value: Swish, σ(t) = t/(1 + e^(−t))
Constructed using the stated vector a and M = 100

rows.measure: Loss at the constructed local minimum compared with a lower-loss point
rows.value: The constructed point (v, w) = (1, 1) is a sub-optimal strict local minimum
rows.note: The example is a constructed numerical case; the paper says the activation and output data are chosen to ensure a bad basin.
rows.check: Example 2 fixes Swish and constructs labels yielding a strict local minimum at (v,w) = (1,1). It reports no training runs or width comparison. The note should say labels are constructed for the fixed Swish activation.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Wide fully connected networks under Theorem 2 and Theorem 3 conditions
reader_labels.reason: The paper proves no sub-optimal basins for the specified wide architectures, as recorded in R1 and R2; it does not test gradient-descent frequency or the teacher-student setup in V2.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Narrow networks with constructed data, and positive homogeneous activations at any width
reader_labels.reason: Bad basins can exist for some narrow-network settings, while positive homogeneous activations have no set-wise strict local minima regardless of width, as recorded in R3–R6.
